output.brief: First-contact resolution fell because of the 14 April Finance change. It cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25 and automatically refers larger cases to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% that same week. Referred calls resolve only about a third of the time, against 82% for the rest, and customers then call back to ask for status. This matches the timing and the size of the drop. The new starters are not the cause. Their referral rate and tenure-level results match the experienced agents, and experienced agents' resolution fell by the same amount. The IVR change came two weeks after the drop, and tariff calls still resolve at 85%. Workload is not tested, so I'm unsure about it. I'm fairly confident (about 85%) in the Finance-change explanation. Don't put the April starters on performance plans, and don't pause the IVR work on this basis. Agree a revised credit limit with Finance, with post-call sampling of credits, and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Track resolution and the rate of unsupported credits before rolling out wider. Finance has said it would consider this if unsupported credits stay under 1% of value. A multi-month dashboard rebuild can wait, since MI can rerun the breakdown for chosen teams within a day.
